text.label: Text: The problem
text.value: The problem

text.label: Text: You are sending your audience to a page that loses them.
text.value: You are sending your audience to a page that loses them.

text.label: Text: Most coaches, authors and influencers either have no website
text.value: Most coaches, authors and influencers either have no website of their own, or one that was built once, years ago, and never updated. Some send people to a link-in-bio page they do not even own. It looks fine on a laptop. It loads slowly on a phone, which is where nearly every follower actually sees it. Think about what that follower just did. They watched you, liked what you said, and went looking for more. That is the hardest thing in this whole business to earn. Then the page they land on makes them wait, or hands them a list of links and leaves them to figure it out alone.

text.label: Text: It does not say clearly what you teach,
text.value: It does not say clearly what you teach, who it is for, or what happens next. So a follower who was ready to buy gives up and goes back to the feed. You never hear about it. Nobody sends you a message to say your page lost them. They just disappear, and you assume they were never that interested. You do not have an audience problem. You have a page that loses them after they show up, and more videos just send more people to the same place. Fix the place first. Then every video you make has somewhere to send them.

text.value: Think of everything you put out as a road. Every video, every clip, every episode moves a person a little further along it. A road has to end somewhere. For most coaches, authors and influencers it ends at a profile page with a follow button, and a follow button does not pay anybody. Your website is where the road ends. It is the one place a stranger can learn who you are, see what you teach, and hand you money for it.

text.label: Text: What we are.
text.value: What we are.

text.label: Text: My company is a modern day talent agency. Talent used to nee
text.value: My company is a modern day talent agency. Talent used to need radio, TV and somebody to let them through the door. Free social media and a nearly free podcast changed that. Anybody can be seen now. What you still need is somebody behind you who knows how to turn being seen into being paid. That starts with a website you own. It is the first thing my team and I build for you, because self-promotion with nowhere to send people is just noise.

text.label: Text: What a stranger needs.
text.value: What a stranger needs.

text.label: Text: Picture the person who taps your link. They have seen one cl
text.value: Picture the person who taps your link. They have seen one clip, maybe two. They do not know you yet. In their head they are asking four questions, in this order. Who is this? What do they teach? Is it for somebody like me? What do I do next? My team and I write your page to answer those four questions in that order, in your words, on a phone screen. When the page answers them, people stay. When it does not, they leave.

text.label: Text: Something to buy.

text.value: A page that only talks about you is a brochure. Yours has things on it a person can actually buy. Your own e-book sits at the front, because it is the easiest first yes you can offer a follower who is still getting to know you. Behind it sits your program, your course or your coaching. And right on the page is a calendar where a serious buyer can book a call with you, without sending a message and waiting for you to answer.

text.label: Text: Somebody always home.
text.value: Somebody always home.

text.label: Text: Your followers do not keep office hours. They show up late a
text.value: Your followers do not keep office hours. They show up late at night, on a Sunday, in the middle of your own client call. So an AI employee lives on your website. It knows what you teach, who it is for and how your program works. It answers the visitor's questions in plain words, in seconds, takes their name and number, and puts a call on your calendar. The visitor gets their answers right away, and a call lands on your calendar.

text.label: Text: Why a book.
text.value: Why a book.

text.label: Text: You already know enough to fill a book. The trouble is where
text.value: You already know enough to fill a book. The trouble is where it lives right now. It is in your head. It is spread across all your videos, which nobody will ever watch in order. It is in the answers you type out to the same questions every week. None of that can be bought. A book is the simplest way I know to take what you know and turn it into a product a stranger can pay for today. Packaging what you know so it can be sold is the heart of what a talent agent does, and this is where we start.

text.label: Text: How it gets out of you.
text.value: How it gets out of you.

text.label: Text: You do not sit down and write it. Writing a whole book alone
text.value: You do not sit down and write it. Writing a whole book alone is slow, and it is easy to stall. We sit down with you and you talk. We ask what you teach first, what comes second, where people get stuck, and what you wish every new client already knew. We record all of it. What you have been saying out loud for years becomes the raw material, and my team does the work of turning it into a book.

text.label: Text: What we build.
text.value: What we build.

text.label: Text: We put what you said into chapters, in an order a reader can
text.value: We put what you said into chapters, in an order a reader can follow from the first page to the last. It is written to sound like you, not like a textbook. We design the cover in your colors with your name on it. We lay it out so it reads well on a phone, because that is where your followers will open it. You read every chapter before anybody else does, and nothing goes out until you say it is right.

text.label: Text: Where it lives.
text.value: Where it lives.

text.label: Text: Your e-book gets its own page on your website. That page say
text.value: Your e-book gets its own page on your website. That page says what is inside, who it is for and what the reader will be able to do when they finish. There is a button to buy it, and the money comes to you. It is sold, not handed out. A reader who paid has a reason to finish. I sell mine on my website the same way. Yours works exactly like it.

text.label: Text: What it does for you.
text.value: What it does for you.

text.label: Text: A follower who has only seen your clips is still a stranger.
text.value: A follower who has only seen your clips is still a stranger. A reader who paid for your book and finished it is not. They know how you think. They have tried a piece of what you teach. By the last chapter they are asking what comes next, and the last chapter tells them: your program, your coaching, a call with you. The book does the long explaining so you do not have to do it one message at a time.

text.label: Text: Something to hold up.

text.value: The book also gives every video a point. Before, you ended a clip by asking people to follow you. Now you end it by telling them where to get the book. Every clip, every episode and every interview you do has the same simple next step, and that step ends on your website. It changes how you are introduced, too. You are the person who wrote the book on it.

text.label: Text: Why a podcast.
text.value: Why a podcast.

text.label: Text: A short clip earns you a few seconds of somebody's attention
text.value: A short clip earns you a few seconds of somebody's attention. Trust takes a lot longer than that. People need to see you and hear from you seven to ten times before they will pay you. A podcast is how you get that time. Somebody puts you on in the car or at the gym and stays with your voice for a whole episode. No clip can do that. One good episode can count for a lot of those seven to ten times.

text.label: Text: What stops most people.
text.value: What stops most people.

text.label: Text: A podcast costs next to nothing to put out. What stops peopl
text.value: A podcast costs next to nothing to put out. What stops people is the technical work. Getting the sound right. Editing. Making the cover. Getting the show onto Apple and Spotify and keeping it there. Writing a title and a description for every episode. None of that is hard for people who do it every day, and that is what my team does. You never touch any of it.

text.label: Text: What you do.
text.value: What you do.

text.label: Text: You sit down and talk about what you know. Sometimes alone,
text.value: You sit down and talk about what you know. Sometimes alone, sometimes with a guest. We help you plan what each episode covers, so you are never staring at a microphone wondering what to say. You already answer these questions every week for your followers and your clients. This is the same conversation, recorded once, so it can keep working long after you have finished talking.

text.label: Text: What we do.
text.value: What we do.

text.label: Text: We take the recording and clean it up. We edit it, fix the s
text.value: We take the recording and clean it up. We edit it, fix the sound, add your opening, and make the cover in your colors so the show looks like it belongs to you. We write the title and the description. We put the episode out everywhere people listen. And we give every episode its own page on your website, with the episode ready to play and a plain write-up of what you covered.

text.label: Text: Why it lives here.
text.value: Why it lives here.

text.label: Text: On a listening app, somebody hears you and moves on to the n
text.value: On a listening app, somebody hears you and moves on to the next show. On your website, the episode sits one tap away from your e-book and your calendar. Each episode page is also one more page Google and the AI answers can read. When somebody types in the exact question you answered on the show, your page can come up, and they arrive at a place you own with something to buy.

text.label: Text: Guests bring people.
text.value: Guests bring people.

text.label: Text: A show gives you a reason to call people you would never oth
text.value: A show gives you a reason to call people you would never otherwise get on the phone. You invite somebody your audience respects. They sit down with you. When they share the episode with their own followers, new people meet you for the first time, and they meet you as the host. Everybody in your field is a peer, and a podcast is the easiest way there is to start working with them.

text.label: Text: One recording, many uses.
text.value: One recording, many uses.

text.label: Text: Here is the part that saves your time. That one recording do
text.value: Here is the part that saves your time. That one recording does not stay one recording. It is the raw material for the next system in the Revenue Engine, which turns it into a steady flow of clips across every platform. So one recording of you talking becomes an episode on your website and a steady flow of clips, and every one of them points back to the same place.

text.label: Text: If that scares you.
text.value: If that scares you.

text.label: Text: I will say it plainly. If having your own podcast and your o
text.value: I will say it plainly. If having your own podcast and your own product scares you, we are not the right fit. You do not need to be polished. You do not need a radio voice or a studio. You need to know your subject and be willing to talk about it out loud. My team and I handle the rest. But you do have to show up, because the whole model runs on people hearing from you.

props.text: If your Google profile is your website, you are renting.

A Google profile, a Facebook page and a link-in-bio page are good things to have. They are not a business. You do not own any of them, you cannot change how they work, and everything a follower does on them happens on somebody else's terms. Your name sits in a list, right beside everybody else who teaches what you teach. The company that owns the page decides what people see first, and it is not always you. Here is what that costs you, one piece at a time.
No form you own, no number you capture, no way to text somebody back. A person taps through, looks around and leaves, and you never learn they were there.
There is nowhere to put instant follow-up, because there is no inquiry to follow up on. Every lead depends on you being free at the moment it lands.
You earned them. They sit on a page that also lists everybody else who teaches what you teach. On your own site those same reviews sell for you, with nobody else on the screen.
When somebody asks ChatGPT who teaches what you teach, the answer is built out of websites it can read. No site, no mention.
No way to know which video, clip or episode brought a buyer to you. Everything is a guess, so every hour you put in is a guess.
A suspended page, a changed policy, a lost login. Twenty years of work sitting on ground you never owned.
None of that is an argument against your Google profile.

Keep it. Feed it. It is free, and it helps people find you. The same goes for every social page you have. But each one should point at something you own. A site that answers the questions, takes the person's name and number, replies in under a minute, and shows your reviews with nobody else beside them. A site with your own e-book for sale on it and your own podcast playing on it. The profile brings them. The videos bring them. Your website is what closes them.
